why_the_passes_missed_it.found: The correct post WAS found, scored, and rejected. It is recorded in the restoration queue as potential_blog_matches[0] with verdict 'partial'.
why_the_passes_missed_it.gate: restore_from_blog.py body_gate: mint only if head_containment >= 0.75
why_the_passes_missed_it.cause: THE TRUTH TITLE CONTAINED THE DOI. The queue's title for this work is 'LLM Hallucination Incident Report — LLM-2025-1222-HALLU ├── DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18368527 — Crimson Hexagon Archive', which tokenises to include 18368527, 5281 and zenodo. Those three tokens CANNOT APPEAR in the blog post, because the blog post predates the Zenodo deposit by five weeks — it was published 2025-12-22 and deposited 2026-01-28. The gate therefore required the source to cite an identifier that did not exist when the source was written. Recomputed now: head_containment 0.67 against a 0.75 threshold; strip the three impossible tokens and it is 0.89, comfortably over. The post also opens INCIDENT REPORT — LLM-2025-1222-HALLU while the deposit title opens LLM Hallucination Incident Report, so the shared tokens sit later in the head and the 800-character window weakened further.
why_the_passes_missed_it.second_cause: doi_in_post was False for the same reason, which cost the fallback route: the 'strong' verdict also accepts doi_in_post AND body_containment >= 0.5, and body_containment was 0.57. A post that could not possibly contain its own future DOI failed both the primary gate and its alternate.
why_the_passes_missed_it.class: This is not a one-record miss. Any work whose queue title carries its DOI, and whose blog original predates the deposit, is scored against tokens the source cannot hold. The gate was built to stop fuzzy matches seating wrong text — it is a good gate, and it was measuring the deposit's metadata rather than the work.
